extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent owners, third‑party requesters, and practitioners involved in inter partes reexamination appeals
extracted.subtask_short: inter partes reexamination briefs and answers
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive requirements for respondent briefs, examiner's answers, and rebuttal briefs in USPTO inter partes reexamination appeals, including content, timing, procedural handling, and how rejections/determinations must be explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing respondent brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an appellant’s brief has been properly filed, any respondent brief must be filed by respondent within one month from the date of service of the appellant’s brief; the time may not be extended (37 CFR 41.66(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant's brief was not properly filed but a notice of non-compliance is mailed, a respondent may file within one month from service of the amended appellant’s brief/non-compliance notice. Failure to timely file will result in the respondent brief not being considered (may be placed in file but marked 'not entered'). A fee (37 CFR 41.20(b)(2)) is required when filed for the first time in a proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file/respondent brief frequency and signature/fee requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent(s) may file a respondent brief once within the time limit; the brief must be signed by the party or the party’s authorized attorney or agent and accompanied by the requisite fee (37 CFR 41.68(a)(1)-(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requester’s respondent brief may not address the brief of any other requester. Ensure correct signature and fee to avoid informality notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief limited scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent brief shall be limited to issues raised in the appellant brief to which the respondent brief is directed (37 CFR 41.68(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent may include arguments previously made of record or supporting the examiner’s findings with respect to claims addressed in the opposing party’s appellant brief, but may not propose new grounds of rejection (especially requester respondents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief — Real Party in Interest statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent brief must include a statement identifying by name the real party in interest (37 CFR 41.68(b)(1)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner’s answer must also acknowledge real parties in interest for each brief (see Examiner’s Answer requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief — Related appeals/interferences/trials statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a statement identifying by application, patent, appeal, interference, or trial number all other prior and pending appeals, interferences or judicial proceedings known to respondent which may be related to or bear on the Board’s decision; copies of any decisions must be included in an appendix (37 CFR 41.68(b)(1)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items belong in a 'Related Proceedings Appendix' when included; examiner’s answer must mirror this identification and include copies where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief — Status of claims statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement accepting or disputing appellant’s statement of the status of claims; if disputed, specify errors with particularity (37 CFR 41.68(b)(1)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If respondent disputes appellant’s status statement, the respondent must identify the precise errors rather than merely asserting disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief — Status of amendments statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement accepting or disputing appellant’s statement of the status of amendments; if disputed, specify errors with particularity (37 CFR 41.68(b)(1)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are no amendments, so state. Disputes must be particularized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief — Summary of claimed subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement accepting or disputing appellant’s summary of the subject matter defined in each independent claim involved; if disputed, specify the errors (37 CFR 41.68(b)(1)(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disputing, explain precisely why appellant’s summary is incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief — Issues to be reviewed on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement accepting or disputing appellant’s statement of the issues presented for review; if disputed, specify the errors; a counter-statement of the issues may be made (37 CFR 41.68(b)(1)(vi)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new ground of rejection can be proposed by a requester respondent. Treat each issue under a separate heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief — Argument requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement accepting or disputing the contentions of appellant with each of the issues presented; if disputed, specify errors and state the basis with citations of statutes, regulations, authorities, and parts of the record relied on (37 CFR 41.68(b)(1)(vii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each issue and counter-stated issue must be treated under separate headings; arguments should cite authority and record locations. Errors must be particularized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief — Evidence appendix rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent’s brief may include an appendix containing only those portions of the record on which reliance has been made; the evidence appendix should contain copies of evidence submitted pursuant to §§ 1.130–1.132 or other evidence entered by the examiner and relied upon (37 CFR 41.68(b)(1)(viii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to unentered evidence is not permitted. See § 41.63 for evidence submitted after appeal. The appendix must state where in the record the evidence was entered by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief — Related proceedings appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing copies of decisions rendered by a court or the Board in any proceeding identified under related appeals/ interferences (37 CFR 41.68(b)(1)(ix)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include copies of cited decisions in this appendix as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief — Certificate of service
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification that a copy of the respondent brief has been served in its entirety on all other parties to the reexamination proceeding, indicating names and addresses of parties served (37 CFR 41.68(b)(1)(x)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A missing certificate of service is an informality that will trigger a non-extendable correction period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new or non-admitted amendments/affidavits/evidence in respondent brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence (37 CFR 41.68(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.116 and § 41.63 for filings after final action or after appeal. New references or evidence not previously entered cannot be relied on in the respondent brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and one-month non-extendable correction period for informalities
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief (appellant’s or respondent’s) does not comply with requirements, the party will be notified of reasons for non-compliance and given a non-extendable time period (one month) within which to file an amended brief (37 CFR 41.67(d); 41.68(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the party fails to timely file an amended brief or the amended brief does not overcome all reasons, consequences differ: appellant’s appeal may be dismissed; respondent’s brief will not be considered (though may be placed in the file but marked 'not entered'). Common defects include missing fee, missing signature, fewer than required copies, no proof of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of briefs and role of CRU and appeal conference
rubrics_metrics.description: All appellant and respondent briefs are processed by the Board and the proceeding forwarded to the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU); the CRU forwards to the examiner after briefs are filed or time has expired, and the examiner should consider the case for appeal and prepare for an appeal conference (MPEP § 2676).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should formulate initial opinion whether an examiner’s answer should be prepared or prosecution reopened. Appeal conference procedures per MPEP § 1207.01; examiner must review the case, be prepared to discuss issues raised in all briefs and propose how to address each issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer — scope and obligation to respond to briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary examiner may furnish a written answer to appellant and/or respondent briefs explaining the invention, references relied on, grounds of rejection, and reasons for patentability; the answer should provide a written statement in answer to each appellant and each respondent brief (37 CFR 41.69 and MPEP guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner’s answer should call attention to errors in appellant’s copy of claims, report conclusions on affidavits/declarations/exhibits admitted to the record, and include rebuttal of all arguments in the briefs. If a ground or reason is not addressed, the proceeding will be remanded by the Board to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new grounds of rejection or new determinations in examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s answer may not include a new ground of rejection, nor may it include a new determination not to make a proposed rejection; any such new ground or determination must be made in an Office action reopening prosecution (37 CFR 41.69(b)-(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner’s answer must include an explicit statement that it does not contain any new ground of rejection or new finding of patentability; if examiner withdraws a rejection or determination of patentability, prosecution must be reopened and appropriate Office action prepared (consult CRU SPRS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer — required items (A–N)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer must include, in the order indicated, items such as: Real Party in Interest; Related Appeals and Interferences; Status of Claims; Status of Amendments; Summary of Claimed Subject Matter; Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal (with subheadings); Findings of Patentability to be Reviewed (with subheadings); Claims Appendix; Evidence Relied Upon; Grounds of Rejection explanations; Determinations of Patentability explanations; explicit no-new-ground statement; Response to Argument; Related Proceedings Appendix; and Period for Providing a Rebuttal Brief (MPEP § 2677 I.(A)-(N)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The answer must follow the order and include subheadings and 'None' where appropriate; failure to include required items can lead to remand or other corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer — listing and subheadings for grounds/findings not on review and non-appealable issues
rubrics_metrics.description: For Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed, the examiner must state whether he/she agrees or disagrees with grounds set forth in briefs and include subheadings: 'Grounds of Rejection Not On Review' and 'Non-Appealable Issues' (and similarly for Findings of Patentability) (MPEP § 2677 I.(F)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State 'None' where appropriate. This delineation helps the Board and parties know which rejections/findings remain but are not presented for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims appendix correctness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must state whether the copy of the appealed claims contained in the appendix to the appellant briefs is correct, and if any claim is not correct, provide a copy of the correct claim (MPEP § 2677 I.(G)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claim text in appendices matches the record; correct copies must be provided if discrepancies exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence relied upon — listing and prohibition on applying new references in answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must list the evidence relied on (patents, publications, Official Notice, admitted prior art) and, for nonpatent references, provide relevant pages; new references cannot be applied in an examiner’s answer—if new references are to be applied, prosecution must be reopened (MPEP § 2677 I.(H) and 37 CFR 41.69(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both art relied upon by the examiner and art relied upon by third-party requester(s) for proposed rejections should be listed. If new references are necessary, reopen prosecution rather than including them in the answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection explanations — 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph (written description/enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, the examiner’s answer must explain how the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 is not complied with, including how the specification and drawings do not describe the subject matter and/or would not enable a person skilled in the art without undue experimentation (MPEP § 2677 I.(I)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include consideration of undue experimentation factors (see MPEP § 2164.01(a)). Explain specifically how spec/drawings fail to describe/enable each rejected claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection explanations — 35 U.S.C. 112 second paragraph (definiteness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, the examiner’s answer must explain how the claims do not particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter (MPEP § 2677 I.(I)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete explanations identifying claim language that fails to meet the definiteness standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection explanations — 35 U.S.C. 102 (anticipation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102, the examiner’s answer must explain why the rejected claims are anticipated, pointing out where all specific limitations recited in the rejected claims are found in the prior art relied upon (MPEP § 2677 I.(I)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific locations (page/col/line/drawing) in the reference where each claim limitation appears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection explanations — 35 U.S.C. 103 (obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103, the examiner’s answer must state the ground of rejection, point out where each specific limitation is found in the prior art, identify differences between the rejected claims and the prior art (primary reference), and explain why it would have been obvious to modify the primary reference to arrive at the claimed subject matter (MPEP § 2677 I.(I)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the rationale for combining references and why the combination would have been obvious to a person of ordinary skill at the time of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-by-feature comparison when correspondence unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: Where questions remain as to how limitations in the claims correspond to features in the art, the examiner must compare at least one rejected claim feature-by-feature with the art relied upon, aligning claim language side-by-side with references to specific page/column/line/drawing reference and quotations as appropriate (MPEP § 2677 I.(I)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This comparison should be explicit and precise to show where each limitation is found or why it is not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanations for other rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection other than those specifically enumerated (112/102/103), the examiner’s answer must specifically explain the basis for that particular rejection (MPEP § 2677 I.(I)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor explanations to the legal basis of the rejection and cite record/reference support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinations of patentability — required explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: For each determination of patentability (inapplicability of a proposed rejection), the examiner’s answer must provide a clear explanation why the proposed-for-rejection claims are not subject to the proposed rejection, with parallel, specific requirements for 112(1), 112(2), 102, 103 (MPEP § 2677 I.(J)(1)-(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain which claim limitations are not found in the proposed-rejection art, identify differences, and explain why the claimed subject matter is patentable; if the requester’s rejection is a combination, explain rationale for not making that combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit statement that examiner’s answer contains no new ground/new finding
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer must provide an explicit statement that it does not contain any new ground of rejection, nor any new finding of patentability (MPEP § 2677 I.(K)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This serves as reminder to the examiner and notification to parties; if a new ground/new finding is made, prosecution must be reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to argument requirement in examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer must state whether the examiner disagrees with each contention of appellants and respondents and explain the reasons for disagreement; if any ground of rejection or inapplicability is not argued/responded to by the appropriate party, examiner must point out each claim affected (MPEP § 2677 I.(L)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reasoned explanations and cite the parts of the record supporting the examiner’s position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period for filing rebuttal brief set by examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer will set forth the period (one month) for the appropriate appellant(s) to file a rebuttal brief after the examiner’s answer; no further papers will be permitted after the rebuttal brief (MPEP § 2677 I.(N)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 41.66(d) limits rebuttal briefs to one month and the time may not be extended; no new evidence or amendments in rebuttal briefs are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer timing, preparation, signing, and review workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer is to be completed within two weeks after the appeal conference, signed by the examiner, initialed by each conferee, reviewed by CRU SPRS/TC QAS, and forwarded to CRU technical support staff for mailing (MPEP § 2677 II.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before preparing the answer, ensure all approved amendments have been physically entered by CRU. If the answer contains a new interpretation of patent law, forward case, answer and memorandum to CRU Director (see MPEP § 1003).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initialing and mailing formalities for examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Each conferee present at the appeal conference places initials below the examiner’s signature on the answer; CRU technical support staff mails the answer to the patent owner and third party requester(s) and attaches form PTOL-2070 for requester mailing (MPEP § 2677 II.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initialing does not necessarily indicate concurrence. Proper clerical processing must be ensured before forwarding to CRU SPRS/TC QAS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of RAN and PTOL-2291 for examiner’s answers when multiple adverse briefs present
rubrics_metrics.description: When at least two adverse parties filed briefs, examiners may use PTOL-2291 to incorporate by reference the Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) including grounds of rejection and determinations; with CRU Director approval, examiners may provide additional explanation as an attachment (MPEP § 2677).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For other situations, examiners are encouraged to incorporate RAN statements by reference where appropriate. Always ensure no new ground/new determination is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to indicate superseding positions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner states a position in the answer that represents a shift from the RAN, the answer must indicate that the last stated position supersedes the former (MPEP guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state which position controls to avoid confusion and potential remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal brief timing and one‑time filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any appellant may file one rebuttal brief within one month of the date of the examiner’s answer; the time may not be extended (37 CFR 41.66(d); 41.71(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebuttal briefs must be timely; late rebuttal briefs will not be considered and will be subject to the same non-compliance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal brief restrictions on new matter and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal briefs (owner or requester) shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit, or other evidence; requesters may not propose new grounds of rejection (37 CFR 41.71(b)-(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.116 and § 41.63 or § 1.116(d) and § 41.63(c) for permissible filings after final action or after appeal. Rebuttal briefs must certify service on all parties (37 CFR 41.71(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal brief certification of service and non-compliance correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal brief must include a certification that it has been served in its entirety on all other parties and list names/addresses; if a rebuttal brief does not comply, party is notified and given a non-extendable one-month period to file an amended rebuttal (37 CFR 41.71(d)-(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amended rebuttal brief is not timely or fails to overcome defects, the rebuttal brief will not be considered.
